pinev: GNIS Port Sheldon, on land S of Pigeon Lake (2016 Michigan 1 m lidar). On the lidar the power plant and its round pond lie N of the lake, so the 400 m ring stays on the S (townsite) side; no street grid or maple avenue shows.

The Ottawa House (two storeys, 80 x 150 ft) stood 'not far from the head of Pigeon Lake', on the NE shore per the old company map (Meima 1921, No. III). On 2016 lidar the lake runs about 3 km E of the pin to its head near -86.162, so that shore is far outside the ring; the hotel was only where the company lived, not the cache spot, so the pin stays on the townsite.

src: Grand Rapids Press, 28 Dec 1921, p. 6, 'A Forgotten City by the Lake' No. III, R. C. Meima (Newspapers.com 1111543176)
